title: Chicago house
description: The jack, 808 toms, the one-finger piano riff and the 303 as bass and lead: Chicago, 1985–87.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: The jack
tracks.blurb: From the jacking kick to a raw jack track with a piano riff and a 303.

lessons.title: The jack
lessons.goal: Write the jacking 707 kick pattern Chicago house was built on.
lessons.concept:
Chicago house began in the early 80s at the Warehouse, the club that gave it its name, and on cheap Roland boxes: the TR-707 and TR-808. Its kick does more than four on the floor. A fifth kick on the **"and" of 4** gives the loop a push into the next bar: that stumble is the **jack**.

`"bd bd bd [bd bd]"` keeps a kick on every beat and squeezes two into the last one, so the extra hit lands on the "and" of 4. Claps on 2 and 4 answer it.

tasks.text: Add a fifth kick on the "and" of 4.
Add a part called clap: a 707 clap on beats 2 and 4.
tasks.hint: const clap = s("~ cp ~ cp").bank("RolandTR707"), and stack(kick, clap)

challenge.text: Add quiet 707 closed hats on every 8th.
challenge.hint: const hats = s("hh*8").bank("RolandTR707").gain(.4), and stack it

summary: The jack: four on the floor plus a kick on the "and" of 4.
[bd bd] in the last beat squeezes two kicks into one step.
The TR-707 is the Chicago machine.

lessons.title: Jacking claps and toms
lessons.goal: Double the clap and add 808 toms on the offbeats.
lessons.concept:
Trax Records tracks are busy below the kick: claps that **double** on the way into beat 1, and **808 toms** bouncing on the offbeats. The 808 toms are pitched (low, mid, high: `lt`, `mt`, `ht`), so a tom pattern is almost a bassline.

`"~ cp ~ [cp cp]"` doubles the last clap. `.mask("<1 0>")` lets a part play one bar and rest the next, which is how these records breathe.

tasks.text: Double the second clap: two claps in the last beat.
Add a part called toms: 808 low, mid, low, high toms on the offbeats.
tasks.hint: const toms = s("[~ lt] [~ mt] [~ lt] [~ ht]").bank("RolandTR808").gain(.6), and stack it

challenge.text: Let the toms play every other bar only.

summary: [cp cp] doubles a clap into the next bar.
808 toms (lt, mt, ht) are pitched percussion.
.mask("<1 0>") plays a part every other bar.

lessons.title: The piano riff
lessons.goal: Write a one-finger piano hook in a key.
lessons.concept:
The Chicago piano is a **riff**, not a chord: one finger stabbing a few notes of the scale, repeated until it sticks. Marshall Jefferson’s "Move Your Body" made it the sound of 1986.

`n("0 ~ 3 ~ 5 ~ 3 0").scale(key)` picks scale degrees, so the riff stays in key however you change the numbers. One `const key` at the top keeps every pitched part in tune.

tasks.hint: const key = "C:minor" on the line after setcpm

tasks.text: Add a part called riff: a piano playing scale degrees 0, 3, 5 in 8ths with rests between.
tasks.hint: const riff = n("0 ~ 3 ~ 5 ~ 3 0").scale(key).s("piano").gain(.6), and stack it

challenge.text: Move the whole thing to F minor by changing only the key.

summary: A riff is a few scale degrees, repeated.
Change the key once and every part follows.

lessons.title: 303: bass or lead
lessons.goal: Play the same 303 line low as a bass, then high as a lead.
lessons.concept:
Phuture bought a TB-303 to make basslines, and found its squelch instead: "Acid Tracks" (1987) is the 303 played **wrong on purpose**. The same line works two ways. Low and filtered, it is a bass. An octave up with the filter open, it is a lead.

The octave lives in the scale name: `scale("C1:minor")` is low, `scale("C2:minor")` an octave up. `.lpf` opens the filter and `.lpq` adds the squelch.

tasks.text: Add a part called acid: a sawtooth line in C1 minor, filtered at 400 Hz with resonance 10.
tasks.hint: const acid = n("0 0 7 0 3 0 7 5").scale("C1:minor").s("sawtooth").lpf(400).lpq(10), and stack it

tasks.text: Lift it an octave and open the filter to 1200 Hz: now it is a lead.

challenge.text: Make every note a short pluck.

summary: The octave in the scale name moves the whole line.
Low and filtered: bass. High and open: lead.

lessons.title: The hand-played filter
lessons.goal: Automate the cutoff the way a hand on the knob would.
lessons.concept:
Acid records were played live: a hand on the 303’s cutoff knob, turning it up over a few bars and back down. A **signal** does the turning: `saw.range(300, 2500).slow(4)` climbs from 300 to 2500 Hz over four bars, then jumps back.

A knob is not perfectly smooth. `.segment(8)` samples the signal eight times a bar, so the filter moves in small steps like a hand would.

tasks.text: Replace the fixed cutoff with a 4-bar saw from 300 to 2500 Hz.
Step it: sample the sweep eight times a bar.
tasks.hint: .segment(8) at the end of the acid line

challenge.text: Move the resonance too, on an 8-bar sine between 5 and 20.

summary: saw.range(a, b).slow(4): a four-bar climb and drop.
.segment(n) steps a signal like a hand on a knob.
Sweep resonance on a different length for variety.

lessons.title: Project: A jack track
lessons.goal: Put the jack, the toms, the piano riff and the 303 together.
lessons.concept:
A Chicago track is raw: a jacking 707, 808 toms, one piano riff and a 303 doing the rest. Keep it loose and a little too loud.

One `const key` ties the riff and the acid line together. A hat fill every four bars (`.lastOf(4, …)`) marks the phrase the way a DJ hears it.
lessons.starter:
setcpm(124/4)
const key = "C:minor"
const kick = s("bd bd bd [bd bd]").bank("RolandTR707")
stack(kick)

tasks.text: Add the clap (doubled), 707 hats on 8ths and the 808 toms, and stack them all.
tasks.hint: const clap = s("~ cp ~ [cp cp]").bank("RolandTR707"), const hats = s("hh*8").bank("RolandTR707").gain(.4) and const toms = s("[~ lt] [~ mt] [~ lt] [~ ht]").bank("RolandTR808").gain(.6)

tasks.text: Add the piano riff and the acid line, both in the key.
tasks.hint: const riff = n("0 ~ 3 ~ 5 ~ 3 0").scale(key).s("piano").gain(.6) and const acid = n("0 0 7 0 3 0 7 5").scale(key).s("sawtooth").lpf(1200).lpq(10).octave(2)

tasks.text: Make the hats fill in the last bar of every four.
tasks.hint: .lastOf(4, x => x.fast(2)) on the hats line

challenge.text: Sweep the acid filter over 8 bars.
challenge.hint: .lpf(saw.range(300, 2500).slow(8)) instead of .lpf(1200) on the acid line

summary: A jack track: 707 jack, 808 toms, a piano riff, a 303.
One const key keeps the riff and the acid in tune.
.lastOf(4, f) marks the phrase with a fill.
